The expert perspectives identified in this study suggest that comparative risk framings of e-cigarettes as less harmful than cigarettes, and the social functions of vaping within adolescent peer cultures, may be important considerations in the development of risk communication targeting adolescents.
nefb380713671: Background: Stress may influence decision-making processes relevant to suicidal behavior, yet few studies have examined risky decision-making and expected value (EV) sensitivity under stress longitudinally among young adults at elevated suicide risk. Methods: Participants included 233 young adults (18-30 years) with recent suicide attempts (n=55), suicidal ideation (n=59), psychiatric controls (n=71), and healthy controls (n=48). Hair cortisol concentration, circulating inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-6, IL-10, IL-1ra, TNF-alpha), Stressful Cups Task, and clinical measures were assessed at baseline, 3-, 6-, and 12-month follow-ups. Results: Participants with a history of suicide attempts showed greater reductions in risky choices under stress over time compared to healthy controls. Greater reductions in EV sensitivity under stress relative to neutral conditions predicted subsequent suicidal behavior. Higher C-reactive protein (CRP) was associated with fewer risky choices under both neutral and stress conditions, while higher interleukin-6 (IL-6) was associated with fewer risky choices under neutral conditions. Higher interleukin-10 (IL-10) was associated with greater reductions in risky choices under stress relative to neutral conditions over time. No significant associations were observed for hair cortisol concentrations (HCC). Conclusions: Stress-related changes in risky decision-making and reduced EV sensitivity may contribute to vulnerability to suicidal behavior. These findings highlight the importance of assessing decision-making under stress and examining inflammatory processes as potential mechanisms underlying suicide risk.
n1b5145ea1cf9: Background: Schistosomiasis morbidity still persists in China despite extensive progress towards elimination of new and active infections. Diagnosis of liver fibrosis related to Schistosoma japonicum remains challenging due to the subjective nature of ultrasound grading and the shortage of experienced sonographers in endemic counties. Methods: We developed a deep learning model that grades schistosomal liver fibrosis from a single B-mode ultrasound image without manual delineation of a region of interest. We used 2,921 images from 2,921 adults (aged 18-88 years, median age 54 years; 46.4% female) from a schistosomiasis hospital in Jiangxi Province, China, between 2019 and 2023. Of these, 12.9%, 34.6%, 32.4% and 20.2% had grade 0, 1, 2 and 3 fibrosis, respectively. Fibrosis grades were based on the clinical ultrasound record and re-evaluation by an experienced radiologist according to the Chinese Handbook of Schistosomiasis Control; discordant cases were reviewed by a second radiologist and resolved by consensus. Predictions from four neural networks with different architectures (ResNet-18, EfficientNet-B0, DenseNet-121 and Swin-T) were combined by weighted soft voting, with weights derived from validation performance. Results: For the four-grade task this model achieved a macro-F1 of 0.8527 (95% CI 0.8184-0.8856), an accuracy of 0.8500 (0.8136-0.8818) and a quadratic weighted kappa of 0.9187 (0.8983-0.9373) on a fixed test set of 440 images. For detecting significant fibrosis (grade 2 or 3; test-set prevalence 0.530), sensitivity was 0.9700, specificity was 0.9179, positive predictive value was 0.9300, negative predictive value was 0.9645, and AUROC was 0.9817. The ensemble achieved a higher macro-F1 than each individual backbone. Every ensemble misclassification was to an adjacent grade; no image with severe fibrosis was classified as no or mild fibrosis, or vice versa, whereas each individual backbone made 1-4 errors spanning two or more grades. Conclusions: The model may provide an automated aid for Schistosoma japonicum-associated fibrosis grading and could potentially support screening and follow-up in endemic areas after external validation.
n20ae8cdd70c6: Introduction: Plasma phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) and amyloid-{beta} 42 (A{beta}42) are advancing toward clinical use for Alzheimer's disease (AD), but their reliability can be impacted by preanalytical handling. Although alternative collection tubes with distinct stabilization strategies --P100 (protease inhibitor) and HEMAcollect (hemolysis/platelet-activation minimization) --have been developed to stabilize plasma proteins, how well they preserve these markers remains unresolved; we therefore compared both against fresh standard EDTA tubes. Methods: In 40 participants, plasma p-tau217 and A{beta}42 were measured (Lumipulse) in paired fresh EDTA, P100, and HEMAcollect samples after 5-day ambient storage. We assessed concentration change, rank-order preservation (Spearman {rho}), percentage difference, and diagnostic classification under the p-tau217/A{beta}42 ratio and p-tau217 alone. Results: P100 preserved p-tau217 favorably, with high rank-order correlation ({rho}=0.98) and a modest median change (+12.1%), and its classification agreement with fresh EDTA reached 97.5% using p-tau217 alone. HEMAcollect showed greater p-tau217 signal loss (-57.5%). A{beta}42 was reduced in both tubes (-72.8% P100; -95.5% HEMAcollect) with loss of rank order, so neither preserved the p-tau217/A{beta}42 ratio. Discussion: Stability was tube- and analyte-specific, and P100 consistently outperformed HEMAcollect --preserving p-tau217 rank order while HEMAcollect reduced signal across analytes. Although neither tube preserved the A{beta}42-dependent ratio, P100 shows potential for p-tau217-based workflows. Preanalytical stability must be established analyte by analyte before alternative tubes enter clinical AD diagnosis.
nf2b4495eab79: Introduction Sepsis is a severe health condition that requires rapid and attentive treatment. The rise in sepsis cases reveals a lack of immediate supportive care in the healthcare system. This lapse may be attributed to a delay in sepsis recognition, patient incompatibility with care plan, and conditions that make treatment more difficult. Building on previous research, this paper seeks to explore the correlation between patients with mental health conditions and sepsis development. State how we define quality of sepsis care. Method Data from 2018-2019 from our ED sepsis quality database was analyzed using T-tests, comparing the characteristics, conditions, and quality of sepsis care of dermatologically-septic patients with and without mental health conditions. Results Between January 1, 2018 and December 31, 2019, 584 LIJ ED patients had sepsis that met inclusion criteria for quality review. Of these, 57 (9.8%) had sepsis of dermatologic origin, of which 30 (52.6%) were female (p = 0.4318). The source of sepsis was the lower extremity in 36.8% of mental health patients vs. 68.4% of non-mental health patients (p = 0.045) and sacral decubitus ulcer in 36.8% of mental health patients vs. 5.3% of non-mental health patients (p = 0.004). In neither univariate nor multivariate analysis were there statistically-significant differences in outcomes in patients with vs. without a mental health issue. However, the need for mechanical ventilation trended lower among patients with mental health disorder (p = 0.141) while the outcome of 3-hour bundle met trended higher among that same group (p = 0.11). Discussion Compared to patients with mental health issues, those without mental health issues had higher rates of sepsis due to lower extremity infections and sacral decubitus ulcer infections. None of the outcome variables met statistical significance. However, dermatologic sepsis patients without mental health issues tended to be more sick than those with mental health issues, as gauged by rates of septic shock and ICU admission (both trending toward statistical significance). They also trended toward receiving lower quality care, as measured by adherence with the 3-hour sepsis bundle. Failure to achieve statistical significance might be due to the small sample size. This is likely the case, as, for example, there was a substantial difference in the percent of multi-racial patients between those with (5.3%) vs. without (28.9%) mental health illness, yet even this large difference did not meet statistical significance (p = 0.104).
ncda586db226a: Dyslexia is a common neurodevelopmental condition characterized by persistent difficulties in reading and spelling. Although social and emotional challenges have been reported in individuals with dyslexia, the genetic relationships between dyslexia, social functioning, and well-being remain poorly understood. We combined phenotypic and genetic data from the Lifelines cohort with publicly available genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics. Associations between dyslexia and social traits were examined using a multi-layered approach encompassing complementary methods, including phenotypic correlation analyses, polygenic score (PGS) analyses, linkage disequilibrium score regression (LDSC), and bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR). Correlation analyses revealed significant phenotypic and genetic correlations between dyslexia and several social traits, including lower levels of life satisfaction, higher levels of loneliness, and less collegial support on the work floor. PGS analyses demonstrated that genetic liability to dyslexia predicted lower life satisfaction and reduced support from colleagues in the workplace, whereas none of the social-based PGSs predicted dyslexia. Bidirectional MR analyses provided evidence that genetic liability to dyslexia contributes to increased loneliness and social isolation, while no evidence was found for causal effects of social-interaction or well-being traits on dyslexia. Together, our results consistently supported a directional relationship from dyslexia toward social and well-being outcomes. In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that dyslexia shares genetic influences with social interaction and well-being traits and suggest that genetic liability for dyslexia contributes to adverse (psycho)social outcomes. These results extend the impact of dyslexia beyond literacy-related difficulties and highlight the importance of providing social and structural support to individuals with dyslexia throughout the lifespan.
ndf85fb1b4053: Background. Electrocardiogram (ECG) foundation models are proposed for clinical use and promoted as fair, yet such claims are rarely tested with subgroup-stratified evaluation. We measured demographic disparities across four ECG foundation models, tested whether mitigation removes them, and asked whether the dominant disparity originates in the models or in the data and the clinical task. Methods. We probed frozen embeddings of four architecturally distinct ECG foundation models (ECGFounder, xECG, ECG-FM, DeepECG-SSL) in thirteen cohorts on four continents (5.4 million analysed ECGs, 31 endpoints, six held-out cohorts), stratified by age, sex and race. We examined embedding geometry, tested post-hoc correction, larger labelled training sets, comorbidity exclusion and low-rank fine-tuning, and compared each network with an untrained copy of itself and with logistic regression on classical ECG measurements. Findings. Disparities concentrated on age, not sex or race (median worst-group AUROC gap 0.028 vs 0.004 and 0.016; age exceeded sex in 97% of results) and replicated externally (ED-BWH 30-day MACE AUROC 0.81-0.90 under 40 years, 0.64-0.71 at >=75). Age formed a smooth gradient in the embeddings, whereas sex, though most decodable, carried no gap. No remedy closed it (low-rank adaptation: -0.007 to -0.004). Untrained copies (r=0.81, 102 pairs) and classical measurements (rho=0.90) reproduced the endpoint-specific gaps, and pretraining raised AUROC (+0.067) without changing them. The largest race effect, higher potassium error in Black patients, vanished at matched true potassium. Interpretation. ECG foundation models carry an age-structured disparity that replicates externally and survives mitigation. Because untrained networks and a classical model reproduce it, the results indicate that it is inherited from the age structure of the ECG and its labels rather than created by the models, so switching or adapting models will not remove it. Age-stratified reporting, untrained and classical baselines, and age-specific thresholds and recalibration are therefore needed. Funding. Austrian Research Promotion Agency (FFG; CARDISENSE project, grant FO999922422).
n6488af550d3a: Background and Purpose: Childhood obesity often leads to flexible flatfoot, which negatively affects foot posture, balance, and physical function. While exercise is commonly used in clinical practice, there is limited comparative evidence on plyometric training versus traditional corrective exercises in this population. This study aimed to compare the effects of an 8 week plyometric exercise program versus flatfoot corrective exercises on balance and foot posture in obese children aged 7 to 11 years with flexible flatfoot. Methods: A parallel, non-randomized comparative study was conducted with 120 children recruited from schools in Bengaluru. Participants were allocated to either Group A (plyometric exercises, n = 60) or Group B (flatfoot corrective exercises, n = 60). Both groups trained for 8 weeks (two 40-minute sessions weekly). Foot posture was assessed using the Foot Posture Index-6 (FPI-6), and static balance was measured as center-of-pressure path length using the BTrackS Balance Tracking System before and after the intervention. Results: Both groups demonstrated statistically significant within-group improvements in foot posture and balance after 8 weeks (p < 0.001). However, the plyometric group achieved slightly better improvements in foot posture (statistically significant for the left foot, p = 0.028) and markedly greater gains in balance (median path length: 30.39 cm vs. 37.45 cm, p < 0.001) compared to the corrective exercise group. Conclusions: Both exercise approaches are beneficial for obese children with flexible flatfoot. Plyometric training provides additional advantages in improving dynamic balance and neuromuscular control, supporting its inclusion in pediatric physiotherapy programs. Keywords: Center of pressure; Medial longitudinal arch; Neuromuscular control; Pes planus; Postural sway; Stretch-shortening cycle
na37fc79a338a: Background: Saffron and its constituent crocin have been investigated as adjuncts for metabolic dysfunction. Their effects on longer-term glycemic exposure and fasting indices may differ. Objectives: To assess the effects of saffron and its constituents on glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting glucose, and insulin resistance. Search methods: We searched PubMed Central on June 11, 2025, and PubMed on October 5, 2025. Selection criteria: Randomized controlled trials in humans comparing affron or its constituents with a control for at least four weeks and reporting a relevant glycemic outcome were eligible. Comparisons were selected to isolate the effect of saffron or crocin. Data collection and analysis: We synthesized continuous outcomes as mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), using inverse-variance random-effects models. HbA1c was the primary outcome. Fasting glucose and the homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) were secondary outcomes. Main results: Twelve trials contributed 570 participants to the analyzed comparisons. Populations included adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes, metabolic syndrome or coronary artery disease, and adolescents with obesity and prediabetes. Seven trials (391 participants) reported HbA1c: the pooled MD was -0.25 percentage points (95% CI -0.58 to 0.08; I2 = 61%). Fasting glucose was lower with saffron or crocin across 12 trials (570 participants; MD -16.16 mg/dL, 95% CI -27.02 to -5.31; I2 = 74%). Five trials (212 participants) contributed to HOMA-IR (MD -1.19, 95% CI -2.25 to -0.12; I2 = 80%). Fixed-effect sensitivity analyses gave smaller estimates across the three outcomes. Authors' conclusions: Saffron and crocin were associated with lower fasting glucose and HOMA-IR, whereas the HbA1c estimate remained compatible with both a reduction and little difference. Variation in populations, preparations, and trial sizes limits interpretation of the average effects. Larger trials with standardized preparations and adequate follow-up are needed to establish the persistence and clinical relevance of these findings. Funding: None
n0eff88ca0a2c: Background: Cardiac arrhythmias may remain unrecognized in adults with chronic disease. Established risk scores primarily address atrial fibrillation. Objective: To develop and internally evaluate an electronic health record (EHR)-based machine-learning model to identify patients more likely to receive a documented cardiac arrhythmia diagnosis. Methods: We retrospectively evaluated EHR data (2018-2025) from one healthcare organization among adults with type 2 diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chronic kidney disease, or coronary artery disease. Logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost were compared. XGBoost was selected using internal validation, reduced to 30 features using Shapley additive explanations, and evaluated in a holdout set with data ending one day before the index date. Sensitivity analyses excluded information recorded within 30, 90, or 180 days before the index date. An atrial fibrillation/flutter-specific analysis compared XGBoost with CHARGE-AF and HARMS2-AF. Results: Among 30,356 patients, 6,835 (22.5%) had a qualifying arrhythmia diagnosis. In 3,051 holdout patients, XGBoost achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.894 (95% CI 0.879-0.908) and an area under the precision-recall curve of 0.792 (95% CI 0.763-0.822). At a 0.5 threshold, sensitivity was 0.564, specificity 0.971, and precision 0.857. AUROC remained 0.896-0.897 across earlier cutoffs. In the common score-calculable atrial fibrillation/flutter subset (n = 2,436), AUROCs were 0.883 for XGBoost, 0.712 for CHARGE-AF, and 0.554 for HARMS2-AF. Conclusions: XGBoost demonstrated strong internal discrimination for documented arrhythmias. External validation and prospective evaluation are needed to assess generalizability and clinical utility.
n47f8055eb8fe: Purpose: This exploratory study examined whether an established clinical procedure for determining speech recognition thresholds in quiet, as outlined by the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (1988), could be extended to a competing-noise condition using existing recorded speech materials. The objectives were to determine whether the resulting speech recognition thresholds in noise (SRTinNs) were broadly consistent with findings from established speech-in-noise measures and to examine their associations with pure-tone thresholds. Methods: Twenty-five adults participated in this exploratory study: 15 with sensorineural hearing loss and 10 with normal audiograms. SRTinNs were estimated using an adaptation of the established threshold-seeking procedure with Canadian French monosyllabic words presented against continuous eight-talker babble. SRTinNs were compared between groups, and associations with pure-tone averages were examined among participants with hearing loss. Results: Mean SRTinNs were +7.2 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for participants with hearing loss and +1.7 dB SNR for those with normal audiograms, representing a significant difference of 5.5 dB SNR (p = .02). Among participants with hearing loss, SRTinNs were significantly correlated with conventional pure-tone averages (r = .54, p = .04) and high-frequency pure-tone averages (r = .64, p = .01). Conclusions: The findings provide preliminary support for further investigation of extending an established clinical threshold-seeking procedure to competing-noise conditions. Further investigation of this approach may help expand access to speech-in-noise assessment in linguistic contexts where suitable recorded speech materials are available but dedicated speech-in-noise tests are lacking.
n4348de8a9db9: Pilonidal sinus disease (PSD) is a common, recurrent inflammatory disease of the natal cleft that clusters in families, but few genetic risk loci are known and its relationship with hidradenitis suppurativa (HS), acne and obesity is unclear. We meta-analysed public genome-wide summary statistics from the Million Veteran Program, UK Biobank, FinnGen and Genes & Health (7,868 cases and 1.6 million controls from four ancestry groups). Of 25 genome-wide significant loci outside the MHC, 19 were novel and 21 remained significant after correction for test-statistic inflation. Liability-scale SNP heritability was 13-15%. Fine-mapping resolved the SOX2, PDE9A and KLF5 loci to single likely causal variants and identified a WNT10A missense variant, p.(Phe228Ile), associated with reduced risk. PSD was strongly genetically correlated with HS (rg = 0.76). In genomic structural equation models, the genetic correlation between PSD and body mass index (BMI, rg = 0.33) disappeared once HS was modelled ({beta} = 0.01), whereas an independent component shared with male-pattern balding remained. Local genetic correlation and colocalisation located this overlap: six loci, including the KLF5 and SOX9 regions, shared a causal variant with HS and five with balding, whereas loci shared with BMI harboured distinct causal variants. Expression quantitative trait locus colocalisation implicated SEMA4B in skin and WNT16 in fibroblasts. PSD is therefore a heritable disorder of the hair follicle that shares most of its common-variant liability with HS, with a separate hair-patterning component and a probable indirect association with obesity.
n8e1e148b3821: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is an X-linked recessive disorder involving progressive muscle tissue loss with replacement by fat and fibrotic tissue, leading in most cases to loss of ambulation (LOA) by early to mid-adolescence. We have previously reported the largest DMD genome-wide analysis to date, using N = 419 patients from the United Dystrophinopathy Project (UDP) whose primary DMD mutations are presumed to preclude production of residual dystrophin. We found strong evidence for 6 modifiers of LOA, 4 of which have been validated in zebrafish. Here we follow up by investigating possible gene-gene interactions both in the UDP and in zebrafish. We find strong evidence of interaction effects for 6 gene pairs in the UDP. We were able to test for interaction in zebrafish for one of these pairs, MAN1A1 and ACTN3, finding strong evidence of an interaction effect with apparent rescue of muscle organization to nearly wild-type levels.
n5ec46b64a494: Tandem repeats (TRs), consisting of consecutive repeated units of 1+bp, are highly polymorphic features found throughout the genome that have been shown to have widespread impacts on gene expression and other traits. However, despite their prevalence, TRs are not included as features in polygenic prediction models, which typically focus on common single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). Here, we develop a framework to incorporate TRs into gene expression models, which consider variants in a cis-window around each gene to predict expression levels. Simulation analyses demonstrate that including linear effects of TR copy number as features can result in substantially improved predictions, particularly when high impact causal TRs are poorly tagged by individual SNPs. We applied our framework to train and evaluate SNP+TR expression prediction models in lymphoblastoid cell lines (LCLs) using data from the Geuvadis cohort (n=359 European individuals) and compared these to SNP-only models. Overall, across 2,553 genes for which models trained successfully, we observed that SNP+TR models give significantly improved performance for 78 genes and a mean gain in adjusted R-squared 0.0037 across all genes, with most gains replicating in the independent Gene-Tissue Expression Project (GTEx) cohort. We additionally find that incorporating TRs results in simpler models and improves portability of models when testing on data for 89 Yoruban individuals from Geuvadis. Finally, we extended our models to consider nonlinear effects of TR copy number on expression. Under our nonlinear TR association testing, we identify 2,255 nonlinear significant genes not captured by linear association testing models, and identify exemplar genes, including PALD1, with highly polymorphic TRs for which incorporating their nonlinear effects results in substantially improved gene expression prediction. Overall, these results demonstrate the utility of including TRs in expression prediction models and show promise that they will have similar impact across other models such as polygenic risk scores for complex traits.
n7708cf078d60: The visual evoked potential (VEP) indexes sensory processing, but the neurophysiological basis of altered VEP amplitudes in autism remains unclear. We examined whether reduced VEP amplitude reflects increased trial-to-trial neural variability and whether this variability relates to electrophysiological markers of cortical excitation/inhibition and developmental functioning. Pattern-reversal VEPs were analyzed in 102 typically developing (TD; 44 female) and 105 autistic (AUT; 15 female) children aged 2-12 years. N1 and N1-P1 amplitudes and inter-trial phase coherence (ITPC) were computed. Resting-state periodic alpha activity and aperiodic exponent were derived using spectral parameterization. Associations among VEP, resting EEG, age, and developmental/behavioral measures were assessed using multiple linear regression. AUT children exhibited reduced N1 amplitude and lower ITPC, with marginally reduced N1-P1 amplitude. Higher ITPC was strongly associated with larger N1 and N1-P1 amplitudes, and group differences in VEP amplitudes were no longer significant after accounting for ITPC. Greater periodic alpha activity was associated with higher ITPC and larger N1-P1 amplitude, while a steeper aperiodic exponent was associated with higher ITPC in the pooled cohort. Within AUT children, higher ITPC was associated with better nonverbal development, verbal cognition, and language scores. Reduced VEP amplitudes in autism may primarily reflect increased trial-to-trial variability rather than systematically weaker stimulus-evoked responses. Associations between ITPC and resting EEG measures suggest that cortical excitation/inhibition may contribute to sensory response reliability. These findings identify neural response consistency as a developmentally relevant feature of visual processing in autism.
nd3349cb4a90a: Background: Ankle-brachial index (ABI) is associated with systemic vascular disease, but its incremental predictive value depends on the clinical comparator, endpoint and validation design. Objective: To test whether a bilateral ABI feature block improves a nonlaboratory clinical benchmark for ten-year death from diseases of the heart or cerebrovascular disease, and whether a limited nonlinear learner improves the same chronological evaluation. Methods: We rebuilt public NHANES 1999-2004 examination data linked to the 2019 public-use mortality file. Adults aged at least 40 years with bilateral ABI values in [0.20, 2.50] and ascertainable 120-month status formed a survey-weighted analytic subset. Models were trained on 1999-2002, tuned within development cycles, and evaluated on 2003-2004. Primary models were linear clinical logistic regression, flexible clinical logistic regression, flexible clinical plus ABI regression, and histogram gradient boosting plus ABI. Point estimates used full evaluation weights; conditional intervals used 32-replicate Fay balanced repeated replication with 15 design degrees of freedom. The study was not prospectively registered. Results: The corrected cohort contained 6,807 participants (4,617 development; 2,190 temporal evaluation) and 409 primary events, including 139 in evaluation. Evaluation AUROC was 0.834 for flexible clinical regression and 0.834 after ABI addition. The paired ABI increment was -0.0007 (95% CI -0.0047 to 0.0032); the paired Brier difference was 0.0008 (95% CI -0.0003 to 0.0018). Boosting plus ABI had AUROC 0.822; versus regression with the same predictor block, its AUROC difference was -0.0117 (95% CI -0.0379 to 0.0144). Its Brier difference was -0.000661 (95% CI -0.001322 to -7.53e-08); the upper limit was extremely close to zero. Neither primary hypothesis of improvement in both metrics was supported. Conclusions: In this corrective, exploratory chronological benchmark, bilateral ABI did not improve discrimination or Brier score beyond a matched flexible clinical model. The result does not negate ABI associations, establish equivalence, or support treatment decisions. It supports transparent evaluation of incremental information in a new cohort rather than claims of clinical utility.
ndb166d29288c: Background | Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a common cause of ischemic symptoms in patients with angina and non-obstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA), predominantly women. Neutrophils may contribute to CMD via vascular inflammation and endothelial injury. We therefore investigated neutrophils and coronary endothelial cells in women with ANOCA. Methods | In this cross-sectional study, we collected blood samples from ANOCA patients (n=123, 84% women) undergoing coronary function testing. Complete blood counts (CELL-DYN, n=123) and neutrophil activation (AQUIOS, n=76) were assessed. Isolated neutrophils were profiled using single-cell RNA-seq (n=11). Guidewire-derived coronary endothelial cells (n=7) isolated during coronary function testing were cultured to passage 2 for bulk RNA-seq. Results | Of 103 women with ANOCA, 23 (22%) were diagnosed with CMD (CFR<2.5). These women showed higher NT-proBNP than women without CMD (234 [136-416] pg/ml vs. 112 [79-200] pg/ml, p<0.001). Neutrophil counts, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio and systemic immune-inflammation index were higher among women with a lower coronary flow reserve (CFR). The proportion of activated neutrophils (CD62Ldim) was inversely associated with CFR at baseline. Single-cell RNA-seq identified four neutrophil clusters, including interferon (IFN)-activated and immature neutrophils. The IFN-activated cluster was expanded in patients with lower CFR and its proportion was inversely associated with surface CD62L expression. Immature neutrophils showed reduced translational and increased inflammatory gene expression in patients with low CFR. Coronary endothelial cells from patients with increased CD62Ldim neutrophils showed higher proliferative/metabolic and lower IFN, complement and coagulation pathway activity. Conclusion | Reduced CFR in women with ANOCA is associated with neutrophil activation, expansion of an IFN-activated neutrophil population, and altered immature neutrophil transcriptional programs. Neutrophil activation is accompanied by distinct endothelial signatures. These findings implicate neutrophil?endothelial interactions in CMD and identify IFN-associated neutrophil states as targets for mechanistic investigation.
n0c2874fda17c: Background: Tobacco smoking is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in the United States, yet its longitudinal association with emergency room (ER) utilization remains understudied. We examined whether cigarette smoking, smoking intensity, and smoking trajectories were associated with subsequent ER use. Methods: We analyzed adult respondents from Waves 1-6 of the Population Assessment of Tobacco and Health Study. Wave 1-3 smoking status, intensity, and cigarettes/day were examined in relation to next-wave ER outcomes. Logistic generalized estimating equation models were used for any ER visit and frequent ER use (>=2 visits), and negative binomial models were used for ER visit count. Trajectory analyses examined Wave 1-5 smoking patterns and Wave 6 ER outcomes, with Wave 1-4 to Wave 5 as sensitivity analysis. Marginal structural models (with IPW) and propensity score matching were used to strengthen causal interpretation. Models adjusted for demographics, insurance, self-rated health, and baseline ER use. Survey weights with balanced repeated replication and Fay's adjustment were used. Results: In adjusted GEE models, current smoking was associated with higher subsequent ER utilization, including any ER visit (OR 1.128, 95% CI [1.068-1.191]), frequent ER use (OR 1.275, 95% CI [1.185-1.372]), and ER visit count (RR 1.264, 95% CI [1.160-1.377]; all p<0.001). Smoking intensity showed a dose-response pattern: smoking <20 cigarettes/day was associated with any ER visit (OR 1.130, 95% CI [1.060-1.204]), frequent ER use (OR 1.231, 95% CI [1.124-1.347]), and ER visit count (RR 1.262, 95% CI [1.110-1.435]), while smoking >=20 cigarettes/day showed stronger associations with any ER visit (OR 1.231, 95% CI [1.127-1.345]), frequent ER use (OR 1.447, 95% CI [1.293-1.618]), and ER visit count (RR 1.368, 95% CI [1.245-1.504]; all p<0.001). Each additional cigarette/day was also associated with higher ER utilization (OR/RR range, 1.007-1.011; all p<0.001). Findings were consistent in marginal structural models and propensity score matched analyses. In trajectory analyses, new/intermittent and persistent smokers had significantly higher ER utilization, while former/intermittent smokers and sustained quitters did not differ from non-smokers, suggesting that this harmful association was eliminated by smoking cessation. Conclusions: Smoking, heavier intensity, and persistent or emerging smoking patterns were associated with higher subsequent ER utilization, while smoking cessation reduces ER risk to the same level as non-smokers. This supports smoking prevention and cessation as strategies to reduce acute healthcare burden.
n1ad37834fade: Background: Observational studies have suggested that metformin lowers breast cancer risk, but many were susceptible to immortal time and time-window bias. Imeglimin, a structurally related glucose-lowering drug approved in Japan in 2021, has been proposed as a candidate for cancer prevention. Methods: We searched PubMed (1 November 2026) and the reference lists of earlier meta-analyses for cohort and case-control studies that reported breast cancer-specific estimates for metformin use and incident breast cancer. One report per source population was pooled with a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model. Studies were classified by whether they addressed time-related biases, using a new-user design, time-varying exposure or target trial emulation. For imeglimin, we applied the same criteria in a systematic search of PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov, assessed whether a meta-analysis was feasible, and reviewed non-clinical and structural data. Results: The search identified 368 PubMed records and 28 reports from other sources. Twenty-two reports from 15 source populations were eligible, and 12 independent studies were pooled. The pooled relative risk (RR) was 0.89 (95% CI 0.74-1.07; I-squared = 90.5%). In nine studies that addressed time-related biases, the RR was 1.00 (0.94-1.08; I-squared = 0%). In three that did not, or were unclear, it was 0.69 (0.56-0.84); the between-group difference was Q = 12.78, p = 0.0004. The difference was not significant when the one unclear study was reclassified (Q = 1.15, p = 0.28). For imeglimin, the search returned 218 PubMed records and 10 registered studies, but no clinical study reported breast cancer or any cancer outcome. No meta-analysis was possible. The available evidence consisted of one in vitro study in breast cancer cells, one docking study, and models of other cancers at concentrations at least about 40-fold above clinical plasma levels. A comparative cohort would need about 631 breast cancer events to detect a hazard ratio of 0.80. Conclusions: In studies that addressed time-related biases, metformin use was not associated with incident breast cancer. A meta-analysis of imeglimin and breast cancer is not yet possible, because no clinical study exists and exposure time since approval is short. Its structural relation to metformin does not by itself predict a preventive effect. The next step should be an adequately powered new-user, active-comparator cohort study. Registration: PROSPERO CRD420261301586 (submitted 6 February 2026; registered 1 November 2026). Deviations from the protocol are reported in the Methods.
n489f9f2ac60b: Purpose: To compare multimodal large language models (MLLMs), vision foundation models (VFMs), and contrastive vision-language models (VLMs) for ophthalmic image interpretation with no labeled examples (zero-shot) or as few as 10 labeled examples per class (10-shot). Design: Retrospective benchmarking study. Subjects: 4 public datasets (UCSD, IDRiD, REFUGE, ASOCT-MSDC) and 3 private datasets (OHTS, BPEI-DLS, WashU-OCT) of anterior- and posterior-segment ophthalmic imaging. Methods: Nine AI models were evaluated across 3 architectural families: MLLMs (Qwen3.8-27B, GLM-5.3-Flash, Gemma-4-31B-it), VFMs (DINOv3, RETFound, VisionFM), and VLMs (CLIP, EyeCLIP, SigLIP2). Models were assessed on disease classification, disease risk and severity grading, anatomical assessment, and lesion localization in fundus and OCT imaging. MLLMs were also compared with a 3D VFM (OCTCube-M) for whole-volume OCT classification. MLLMs were evaluated zero-shot and 10-shot, without additional training. Vision models (VFMs and VLMs) were adapted by linear probing and fine-tuning on the same 10-shot set and on the full training dataset (FD). Main Outcome Measures: Disease classification performance (macro-averaged F1, AUROC, quadratic weighted kappa [QWK]), anatomical localization accuracy, and cross-dataset generalization. Results: For retinal OCT disease classification, 10-shot MLLMs achieved a macro-F1 of 0.94, versus 0.59 (10-shot) and 0.96 (FD) for vision models. For diabetic retinopathy and macular edema grading, 10-shot MLLMs achieved QWKs of 0.69 and 0.73, versus 0.48 and 0.57 (10-shot) and 0.72 and 0.79 (FD) for vision models. For lesion localization, 10-shot MLLMs achieved an F1 of 0.75, versus 0.70 (10-shot) and 0.86 (FD) for vision models. For vertical cup-to-disc ratio estimation (OHTS), zero-shot MLLMs achieved a mean absolute error of 0.14, versus 0.21 (10-shot) for vision models. For whole-volume OCT classification (WashU-OCT), zero-shot MLLMs achieved a macro-F1 of 0.71, versus 0.50 (10-shot) and 0.82 (FD) for vision models. Conclusions: Open-weight MLLMs given 10 labeled examples per class outperformed VFMs and VLMs trained on the same examples in most tasks and approached the performance of fully trained VFMs and VLMs in selected disease classification and grading tasks. MLLMs also demonstrated promising zero-shot performance on non-public clinical datasets without task-specific training. By reducing the need for large labeled datasets and task-specific model adaptation, MLLMs could broaden who can develop and validate ophthalmic AI.
n12792d3c18ef: Background: Regular exercise during pregnancy improves maternal and neonatal outcomes; however, the molecular pathways underlying placental adaptations to prenatal exercise remain poorly understood. Klotho is a cytoprotective protein involved in the regulation of oxidative stress, metabolic homeostasis, and cellular resilience, yet whether placental Klotho concentrations are associated with prenatal exercise has not been previously investigated. Aims: The primary aim of this study was to examine whether participation in a supervised concurrent exercise program during pregnancy is associated with placental Klotho concentrations at birth. Secondary aims were to explore potential fetal sex-specific patterns and associations between placental Klotho and selected biomarkers related to angiogenic and inflammatory pathways. Methods: Pregnant women were allocated to either a supervised concurrent exercise program or usual care. The intervention comprised combined aerobic and resistance training performed three times per week from early-mid pregnancy until birth. Placental tissue was collected at birth, and Klotho concentrations were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Secondary analyses explored potential sex-specific patterns and examined associations between placental Klotho, placental weight, and a panel of placental biomarkers. Results: Seventy-six women were included (exercise: n = 41; control: n = 35). Placental Klotho concentrations were significantly higher in the exercise group, with an adjusted mean difference of approximately 101 pg/mL (p = 0.001; partial η 2 = 0.164). This effect was consistent across fetal sex, with no significant exercise-by-sex interaction. Several placental biomarkers were independently associated with Klotho, suggesting a potential relationship with angiogenic and inflammatory signaling pathways. Conclusions: Participation in a supervised concurrent exercise program during pregnancy is associated with higher placental Klotho concentrations at birth, irrespective of fetal sex. These findings provide novel insight into molecular pathways potentially involved in placental adaptations associated with prenatal exercise and reinforce the concept of the placenta as an exercise-responsive organ during pregnancy. Keywords: Concurrent training; Exerkines; Oxidative stress; Pregnancy; Placental function
nfb21b0ae8e53: Background: Diabetes is an increasing public health challenge in India, particularly among middle-aged and older adults. Understanding its prevalence and associated risk factors is essential for informing prevention and management strategies. Objective: This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of diabetes and identify demographic, socioeconomic, behavioural, and health-related factors associated with diabetes among adults aged 45 years and above in India. Methods: A cross-sectional analysis was conducted using nationally representative data from the Longitudinal Ageing Study in India LASI Wave 1 2017 to 18, comprising 72,055 individuals aged 45 years and above. Diabetes status was based on respondents' self-reported diagnosis by a health professional. Descriptive statistics were used to estimate diabetes prevalence, and multivariable binary logistic regression was performed to examine associations between diabetes and selected covariates, including age group, sex, place of residence, caste, religion, physical activity, dietary practices, heart disease, and heart attack risk. Results: Diabetes prevalence was higher among older adults, urban residents, females, and individuals belonging to the Other Backward Classes OBC. After adjustment for potential confounders, age, urban residence, caste, religion, heart disease, and heart attack risk were significantly associated with diabetes, whereas sex was not statistically significant after adjustment. Individuals aged 55 to 64 years and those residing in urban areas exhibited significantly higher odds of diabetes compared with their respective reference groups. Conclusions: Diabetes is highly prevalent among middle-aged and older adults in India and is associated with several demographic, socioeconomic, and health-related factors. These findings highlight population groups that may benefit from targeted prevention, screening, and management strategies. Further longitudinal studies are warranted to clarify temporal relationships and causal pathways.
nf546379dab2f: Objectives: This study aimed to evaluate the ability of VoxelMap, a deep learning framework for 3D respiratory motion estimation, to generate volumetric images in real-time from 2D projections acquired for two deformable lung phantoms on a clinical interventional C-arm angiography system. Materials and Methods: VoxelMap was evaluated using the PixelPrint4D and Casper deformable physical thoracic respiratory phantoms. Four-dimensional cone-beam CT (4D CBCT) images acquired on a clinical fixed-room C-arm angiography system were used for network training and volumetric ground truth. Prediction accuracy was evaluated on withheld respiratory phases using structural similarity index measure (SSIM) and peak signalto-noise ratio (PSNR). Model inference time was measured to assess suitability for continuous real-time processing. Deep ensembles were also used to assess model uncertainty. Correlation between ensemble uncertainty and prediction error was evaluated for both phantoms. Results: VoxelMap achieved high prediction accuracy across withheld respiratory phases in both physical phantoms. SSIM values exceeded 0.92 in all experiments, with a higher performance observed for the Casper phantom (0.969-0.973) than for the PixelPrint4D phantom (0.927-0.943). Model inference times were less than 15 ms for both phantoms which is compatible with real-time processing. Ensemble uncertainty was positively correlated with prediction error in both phantoms, indicating that higher uncertainty was associated with less accurate volumetric predictions. Conclusions: Our study demonstrated that VoxelMap generates accurate volumetric deformations of respiratory anatomy from projections acquired on a clinical interventional C-arm system, with computational inference times compatible with continuous processing. By deriving volumetric information directly from two-dimensional fluoroscopic projections, VoxelMap has the potential to augment continuous fluoroscopic guidance with continuously updated volumetric information. Ensemble uncertainty may provide a potentially useful indicator of prediction reliability. Further studies using clinically representative training data and patient studies is required to establish clinical utility. Our code is available at https://github.com/Image-X-Institute/Voxelmap.
n913ff0215178: AGP1 (α-1 acid glycoprotein) is an acute phase immune response protein recently shown to influence leptin receptor activity and body weight regulation. AGP is a highly glycosylated protein, with 45% of its molecular weight made up by glycans, yet little is known about how the latter responds to metabolic interventions or its role in AGPs immunometabolic function. In this pilot study (n = 26), we evaluated the effect of calorie restriction (CR - 2years, 25% CR in non-obese adults) on N-glycosylation of AGP1. AGP1 has 5 glycosylation sites, of which sites IV and V are dominated by highly branched, fucosylated, and sialylated glycans, and inflammatory conditions are associated with reduced branching at sites IV and V and increased fucosylation. With CR (0 month to 24 month, ~12% CR, weight loss of ~8.2 kg), there was increase in branching at sites IV and V (p<0.05, FDR corrected), and increased fucosylation (p<0.05, FDR corrected). Exploratory moderation analyses suggest that highly sialylated site IV glycans and low-branched site I glycans may influence the relationship between CR and leptin (p<0.05). Overall, AGP glycome is largely remodeled with CR, and it is unknown if these are upstream or downstream of immunometabolic changes seen with CR.
n32813a5ae518: Background Current clinical management of patients with hypothyroidism emphasizes thyroid hormone replacement at doses that normalize serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels. However, biochemical correction does not always translate into symptom resolution or restored health-related quality of life (QoL). We evaluated whether higher TSH levels within the reference range would be associated with worse Thyroid-Related Patient-Reported Outcome (ThyPRO)-39 scores, reflecting greater symptom burden. Objective The objective of this study was to assess residual symptoms and health-related quality of life in women with normal TSH levels in patients with cardiovascular disease being treated for hypothyroidism. Materials and methods We prescreened 96 participants who completed study assessments. Following the TSH obtained at the study visit, 14 participants were excluded due to TSH values falling outside the predefined euthyroid range (0.35-4.94 ?IU/mL), resulting in a final cohort of 82 women. We also investigated whether comorbidities contributed to symptom burden. Results Although mean composite scores were numerically higher in the upper TSH quartiles, neither multivariable regression nor ordered trend testing demonstrated a significant association between increasing TSH and overall symptom burden (Jonckheere-Terpstra p = .333). Notably, major depressive disorder (MDD) (?=16.93, 95% CI 8.22?25.65; p<.001) and hypertension (HTN) (?=12.45, 95% CI 2.24?22.66; p=.018) were independently associated with greater Thy-PRO-39 scores. Conclusions MDD and HTN were independently associated with higher Thy-PRO-39 scores, suggesting that comorbidities may be more strongly related to persistent symptoms than modest variation in TSH within the euthyroid range. Our results suggest that in patients with hypothyroidism and cardiovascular disease, comorbidities may be particularly important when interpreting residual symptoms in biochemically euthyroid patients.
n29b951e66ada: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder affecting roughly one million people in the U.S. People with PD (PwPD) exhibit classic motor symptoms that limit performance on functional tasks and reduce quality of life (QOL). Despite functional ability (FA) being a critical indicator of patient well-being, objective and quantitative measurement of FA during activities of daily living (ADLs) is not a part of standard clinical assessments. To address this gap, we conducted a pilot study of PwPD (n = 39) and healthy controls (n = 7) performing ADLs. We attached nine-axis inertial measurement units (IMUs) to toothbrushes and hair combs to collect continuous acceleration and angular velocity data during toothbrushing and hair-combing tasks. After preprocessing, we visualized signals with kernel density estimation and continuous wavelet transforms, revealing characteristic distributional, temporal, and spectral patterns. We then segmented signals into 3-9 second non-overlapping intervals. From each interval, we extracted 30 features (13 acceleration-derived, 17 angular-velocity-derived) and trained eXtreme Gradient Boosted (XGBoost) classifiers to discriminate disease state and severity, symptom presence, and impaired FA. Notably, models trained on hair-combing data discriminated PwPD from controls (balanced accuracy 0.864) and identified patient-reported impairment in FA (0.869). Models trained on toothbrushing data achieved moderate performance on the same tasks (balanced accuracy 0.752 and 0.686, respectively). These preliminary findings suggest that short-segment IMU data from common ADL implements can quantitatively characterize disease severity and task-specific performance in PwPD, supporting their integration into routine clinical care.
naf4a7d7b0cc1: Introduction Socioeconomic inequities in chronic kidney disease (CKD) outcomes are recognised and greater at early stages, but where exactly inequities arise within early care remains unclear. This distinction is critical: if disparities occur before clinical recognition, strategies focused on management after diagnosis may have limited impact. Methods We conducted a population-based cohort study linking healthcare and Census data for adults in North-East Scotland, 2011-2020. We examined sequential components of early kidney care from initial clinical detection (eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m^2). Exposures were household and neighbourhood deprivation and living circumstances (rurality, living alone, mental health). Components of early kidney care were: prior surveillance; presentation (including late/unmonitored); confirmation/monitoring; treatment initiation; and unplanned emergency care. Adjusted risk ratios were estimated using modified Poisson models. Mortality was assessed up to 10 years using Cox regression with separate short-term (<1 year) and long-term estimates. Results Among 44,252 individuals, inequities were most pronounced at initial clinical detection. Individuals from deprived households were more likely to present late (adjusted RR 1.69, 95% CI 1.48-1.93). Inequities in planned monitoring after presentation were less evident (RR 1.00, 0.95-1.05). Urine albumin testing was infrequent among those with cardiovascular risk factors. Late presentation was also associated with increased mortality (adjusted HR 1.78, 1.70-1.87), persisting beyond the first year. Conclusions Socioeconomic inequities in CKD are greatest at or before initial clinical detection, with late presentation a measurable indicator. Emphasis on primary care monitoring and prescribing is unlikely to reduce disparities if early detection and awareness are not also addressed.
n46a85ffb76d3: The use of mediation analysis is common in epidemiology to decompose an exposure-outcome total effect into direct and indirect effects via a given set of mediators. The counterfactual framework in causal inference allowed for great improvements in mediation analysis to define identification assumptions and clarify sources of bias in different settings. Multiple mediation methods have been proposed to consider confounders of various types and for different settings such as longitudinal designs. However, in some settings we may reasonably expect spatially heterogeneous estimates of both natural direct and indirect effects. In various research areas, especially environmental and social epidemiology, we would expect there to be spatial dependence that could be leveraged. In this paper, we describe and compare a set of approaches to perform spatial mediation analyses and conduct an extensive set of simulations to quantify their performance. We also present a case study assessing the spatially heterogeneous mediating role of PM2.5 in the association between income and cardiovascular diseases. We provide all code via GitHub for replication and reproducibility purposes. We find that using a framework combining geographically weighted regression (GWR) and other spatially varying coefficient (SVC) models and the product method of mediation analysis is accurate and precise at estimating spatially heterogeneous effect estimates and handling spatial confounding in a grid setting. Such spatial approaches can be extended to any mediation approach and various confounding structures.
nfafe5e3d9b49: Background The 1984 Bhopal Gas Leak is widely considered the worst industrial disaster in history, and "big events" can have durable impacts on infectious disease transmission. Among men who have sex with men, we examined whether meeting sexual partners near the original gas leak site was associated with HIV, HIV-associated risk behaviors, and sexual stigma. Methods We used respondent-driven sampling to enroll MSM in Bhopal during 2023-24 (n=750). Participants reported the four locations where they most often went to meet sexual partners in the past year. Sexual stigma was defined by mechanism (enacted, anticipated, internalized) and source (healthcare, family, society). We calculated weighted (RDS-II) prevalences of HIV, population-level HIV viremia ([≥]200 copies/ml), and associated risk behaviors by meeting location type and distance to the original gas leak site. We used weighted logistic regression to examine associations between sexual stigma and partner meeting locations. Results HIV prevalence was elevated among participants meeting near the leak site: 21.7% within 1 km, 14.4% between 1-2 km, and 9.7% over 2 km. Population-level HIV viremia and the proportion of MSM engaging in sex work were also elevated within 2 km. Sexual stigma measures were significantly associated with meeting a partner within 2 km of the leak site. Transportation-related spaces were associated with higher prevalences of HIV and viremia. Conclusions Industrial disasters may create marginal spaces which concentrate individuals facing greater stigma and elevated HIV transmission risk. Venue-based interventions near the gas leak site and at transportation centers may be warranted in Bhopal.
nf06dbb6a3153: Gastrointestinal diagnosis and monitoring rely on colonoscopy, which requires anesthesia and a long wait, and non-invasive alternatives are lacking. Here we show that whole-transcriptome sequencing of stool host RNA, recovering a median of 6300 protein-coding genes across 285 libraries spanning colorectal cancer (CRC) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), precancerous lesions (APL), and normal samples, reads a census of the cells shed into the lumen. In normal samples, epithelium supplies 81% and immune cells supply 11% of stool host mRNA transcripts; the immune cells' share rises in CRC and IBD, and B- and T-cell receptor clonotypes rise with it. In this work, we show that CRC, IBD, and normal samples carry distinct transcriptome profiles, which a three-class model separates with an area under the curve of 0.94-0.96, and that within inflammatory bowel disease a 15-gene neutrophil score tracks endoscopic activity better than fecal calprotectin in the same stool.
n94a267caf5be: Introduction Docetaxel is widely used for advanced and metastatic solid tumours, but dose limiting toxicities, particularly haematological adverse events, often lead to treatment delays, dose reductions or discontinuation and impair quality of life. Tinospora cordifolia (Guduchi), long used in Ayurveda for its immunomodulatory and rejuvenating properties, has shown chemoprotective potential in experimental and early clinical studies, but robust randomized evidence is lacking. This trial evaluates whether adding an aqueous standardized extract of T. cordifolia(AsSET) to docetaxel-based chemotherapy reduces grade [≥]2 adverse events and improves quality of life in patients with advanced or metastatic solid tumours. Methods and analysis This randomized, double-blinded, and placebo-controlled trial designed to evaluate the chemoprotective efficacy of an aqueous standardised extract of Tinospora cordifolia (AsSET) in patients with advanced, recurrent or metastatic solid tumors receiving docetaxel-based chemotherapy. A total of 81 eligible patients that have provided informed consent were recruited in the study. Participants were randomized 2:1 to AsSET or placebo using stratified permuted block randomization, stratified by planned cumulative docetaxel dose ([≤] 225 vs >225 mg/m2), except five participants enrolled before that date were allocated by minimization. All participants received standard intravenous docetaxel-based chemotherapy plus oral administration of either AsSET (two 300mg tablets, 600mg, twice daily) or matching placebo, from enrolment until completion of docetaxel-based therapy. Clinical, laboratory, imaging, and questionnaire based-assessment were performed at baseline, at scheduled interval during treatment and at the final visit. In consenting participants, blood samples for pharmacokinetics were collected once, at nine timepoints up to 24 hours, in any chemotherapy cycle from cycle 2 onwards. Adverse events were graded according to CTCAE version 5.0. The primary outcome is the proportion of patients experiencing grade [≥]2 adverse events from first dose to study completion (up to 24 weeks). Secondary outcomes include quality of life measured by the EORTC QLQ-C30 and the disease-site-specific FACT scale, progression-free survival (PFS) per RECIST v1.1, haematological and biochemical parameters, and pharmacokinetic parameters. The database was locked on 17 September 2026 and the locked dataset was transferred to an independent statistician who remains blinded to treatment allocation. Unblinding has not yet been done and outcome analysis has not started. Ethics and dissemination This study was approved by the Institutional Ethics Committee III (IEC) of the Advanced Centre for Treatment Research & Education in Cancer, Tata Memorial Centre, (ACTREC), Kharghar, Sector 22, Navi Mumbai (project approval no. 900950; first approved on 28 June 2023; this paper describes the most recently amended protocol, version 4.0 dated 24 February 2026; amendments are listed in Annexure 1). The trial is registered with the Clinical Trials Registry-India (CTRI/2023/08/056129) and is conducted in accordance with ICH Good Clinical Practice, the new drugs and Clinical Trials Rules 2019. All participants provided written informed consent, with an additional consent for pharmacokinetic sampling. Participants data are coded to protect confidentiality, and no participant will be identified in any publication without permission. The findings from this study will be presented at an academic conference and published in scholarly journals regardless of the findings.
n8b2bbcee9f73: Background Some patients obtain less benefit than expected from deep brain stimulation (DBS) despite optimized programming. We systematically reviewed the outcomes of surgical revision in this setting. Methods Following PRISMA 2020, we searched PubMed, Embase and Scopus to October 2026 for studies of lead repositioning, replacement, added (rescue) leads or target switching performed for inadequate benefit or stimulation-related adverse effects; revision for infection or hardware failure was excluded. Outcomes were pooled with random-effects models, and certainty was rated with GRADE. Results Seventeen case series (approximately 149 patients) were included. Across 14 studies (95 patients), 81% (95% CI 68 to 91%) improved meaningfully, with similar estimates for same-target revision (82%) and for added or switched leads (79%). In Parkinson disease, the off-medication/on-stimulation motor score fell by 15.6 points after lead revision (95% CI 68 to 91%; four studies). Benefit was greatest when a lead outside the dorsolateral subthalamic nucleus was corrected and levodopa response was preserved. Seven studies reported surgical or hardware complications, and two deaths occurred. Certainty of evidence was very low. Conclusions Most published revised patients improve, but the evidence derives from small uncontrolled series. Revision should follow imaging, hardware checks and exhaustive reprogramming, within multidisciplinary review.
n9497b0d89a82: Brazil experienced a large dengue epidemic during the 2024 season, with almost 5.7 million total cases (compared to under 1.3 million in 2023), raising questions about underlying drivers, including rising temperatures, expansion into susceptible populations, changes in reporting, and novel strains. We compared state-level 2024 incidence with 2000 - 2023 data to quantify anomalies. Nine of 27 states, primarily in the Southeast, recorded their highest incidence in 25 years, accounting for 97% of cases while comprising only 67% of the population. In contrast, nine states (mostly in the North and Northeast) reported below-average incidence. Counterintuitively, the correlation between state-level temperature and incidence declined significantly over the study period, turning negative by 2024 (r = -0.72), a reversal from the positive correlations observed at the start. To determine whether this pattern was driven by northern temperatures being too high for transmission, or by spatial variation in immunity, we fit generalized additive models to effective reproductive numbers. Transmission remained substantial at the highest temperatures, while reproductive numbers declined with lagged cumulative incidences, indicating susceptibility depletion was important. We then estimated state-level susceptibility using a mechanistic SEIR-SEI model, describing a trade-off: high temperatures supported high transmission rates, but were associated with reduced susceptibility. Linear regression models confirmed both temperature and susceptibility were necessary to predict the 2024 outbreaks, suggesting that immunity plays an important role in modulating temperature's effect on incidence. Future surveillance integrating measures of immunity could enhance forecasts and early-warning systems, particularly as climate change expands dengue into immunologically naive populations.
nffb5fa80c57e: Acute intermittent hypoxia (AIH) therapy is a promising neurorehabilitative intervention with well-documented enhancements in motor function in people with spinal cord injury. Its enhancements in lower-limb motor control in multiple sclerosis (MS), where walking impairment is a leading source of disability, remain uncharacterized, and the supraspinal effects of AIH therapy are unknown. In a sham-controlled, double-blind crossover trial ( NCT05164705 ), 23 adults with MS completed 5 sessions of AIH therapy and of sham therapy; magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was performed before and after each therapeutic arm. At each timepoint, blood oxygenation level-dependent (BOLD) functional MRI was collected during a repeated plantar- and dorsi-flexion task. Task-evoked activation was modeled at the group level and compared across timepoint and therapeutic arm. Activation changes differed for the left- and right-foot task. AIH augmented activation in the basal ganglia, thalamus, and cortical motor regions during left-foot movement with similar but sub-threshold patterns for the right foot. Right-foot movement additionally showed enhanced deactivation in prefrontal, parietal, and temporal cortices, although these effects were primarily in white matter voxels, limiting their interpretability. These findings suggest that changes in subcortical activation may contribute to motor function improvements following AIH therapy, implicating the basal ganglia-thalamo-cortical motor loop as a target of AIH-induced neuroplasticity. These results also indicate that AIH therapy modulates supraspinal motor circuitry, supporting further investigation of the cortical and subcortical effects of this emerging therapeutic treatment.
nc35da7b3ae0c: Background: Asthma is a time-sensitive inflammatory disease whose activity exhibits daily (circadian) rhythms. An outstanding question is whether such temporal variations extend to advanced asthma treatments like biologics that are used for moderate-to-severe disease. Objective: To examine how time-of-administration relates to the effectiveness of the anti-IgE biologic, omalizumab. Methods: We performed a retrospective cohort study of omalizumab effectiveness in 153 patients with asthma with timestamped administration records. Time of day was modeled as a continuous variable and dichotomized into morning (8:00-11:59, n=74) versus afternoon (12:00-17:00, n=79) administration. Multivariable logistic regression and Cox time-to-event analyses were used to adjust for key covariates. For biological validation, we treated ovalbumin (OVA)-sensitized mice with anti-IgE antibody at various times of day and measured its impact on inflammatory lung pathology. Results: Receiving the initial dose of omalizumab in the afternoon was associated with better response, defined as a 50% or more reduction in asthma exacerbations in the year after initiation (Odds ratio, OR: 5.20; 95% CI, 1.94-13.96). For each hour later in the day the initial dose of omalizumab was given, the odds of a response increased by 34% (adjusted OR, 1.34; 1.02-1.77). In OVA-sensitized mice, anti-IgE treatment attenuated inflammatory lung pathology, including OVA-induced airway hyperresponsiveness and type-2 inflammation-related gene expression, in a time-of-day-sensitive manner, with maximum effectiveness when dosed in the latter part of the dark phase, functionally analogous to the afternoon in humans. Conclusion: The timing of anti-IgE treatment for asthma may influence therapeutic success. These findings have implications for optimizing the effectiveness of respiratory biologics.
nc30cc8b167fb: Importance: One adult in 10 has consulted a chatbot for health information within 6 months, and nearly half of users do so to decide whether they need care. Referral regardless of need could add demand on stretched services. Objective: To compare referral to a professional by general-purpose language models in health and non-health situations against the level of contact that human raters judged necessary. Design, Setting, and Participants: Cross-sectional study of 4,346 responses generated in September 2026 by 53 general-purpose model configurations, released between March 2023 and September 2026 and accessed through APIs or run locally, to 82 investigator-written messages (41 health and 41 non-health). No patients were involved. Exposures: Health vs non-health scenario. Main Outcomes and Measures: Professional referral, unconditional or conditional on a future change or on doubt, coded by 3 language models and compared with the level of contact that physicians, pharmacists and 2 technically trained raters judged necessary. Results: Referral occurred in 74.7% of health and 46.3% of non-health responses, more often for health in every configuration (standardized difference, 28.3 percentage points; 95% CI, 18.3-37.0). Where raters judged contact unnecessary, 64.5% of health vs 27.6% of non-health responses recommended a professional (odds ratio, 17.08; 95% CI, 6.14-47.54); most of the health excess was conditional referral (46.3% vs 21.0%), and unconditional referral was 18.1% vs 6.6% (odds ratio, 4.66; 95% CI, 1.43-15.19). Where an in-person assessment was judged necessary, referral was similar (89.6% vs 84.5%). In medicines and physical health, referral was not associated with rated severity (odds ratio per point, 1.16; 95% CI, 0.53-2.55), unlike outside health (3.86; 95% CI, 1.79-8.33). The referral gap was 20.5 percentage points among configurations released in 2023 and 32.2 and 32.3 in 2025 and 2026 (4.8 percentage points per year; 95% CI, 2.3-7.2). Conclusions and Relevance: General-purpose language models referred people to a professional where a visit was needed, in health as outside it, but in health also in 2 in 3 situations that physicians and pharmacists judged manageable without contact, a pattern stronger in newer models. Evaluations of these systems should include whether their advice distinguishes situations that can be deferred or managed at a distance, alongside the referral of serious cases.
n7a8cb2f8dd2b: Erectile dysfunction and age-related testosterone decline are common and growing concerns among ageing men, yet current pharmacological options are constrained by tolerability, cost, and reluctance to start hormone-based therapy, leaving a real gap for safe, long-term alternatives. Shilajit, a resinous plant exudate long used in Ayurvedic medicine, is increasingly proposed to fill this gap with its bioactive constituents thought to confer adaptogenic, antioxidant, and androgen-modulating effects. However, clinical support for this use remains thin, with most existing trials small and conducted in healthy men rather than those with diagnosed erectile dysfunction. In this randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial (CTRI/2025/07/090919), 100 men aged 35-55 years with mild-to-moderate erectile dysfunction (IIEF erectile function domain score 11-25) and symptoms suggestive of androgen deficiency were enrolled across two sites. Participants received 250 mg twice daily of standardised TruBlk Shilajit resin or matched placebo for 90 days. Primary endpoints, as registered, were change from baseline in IIEF total and domain scores, total and free testosterone and cortisol, and Hypogonadism Impact of Symptoms Questionnaire (HIS-Q) domain scores. Secondary endpoints included nitric oxide, Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS), and Participant and Investigator Global Assessments. Semen parameters were assessed in a subset of participants. IIEF total score improved significantly more in the TruBlk group (+32.1% vs. +13.6%; d=0.67, p=0.005), with significant gains in four of the five domains, namely erectile function, orgasmic function, overall satisfaction, and intercourse satisfaction (d=0.52-0.61, p=0.011-0.044), while sexual desire showed a smaller, non-significant improvement (d=0.44, p=0.109). This was accompanied by significant increases in total testosterone (+46.1% vs. +10.0%; d=0.44, p=0.030) and free testosterone (+37.4% vs. +6.8%; d=0.41, p=0.048). HIS-Q symptom domains showed a similar pattern to IIEF, with Day 90 differences favouring TruBlk in three of five domains (sexual, energy, and sleep; d=-0.59 to -0.82, p<0.02), while cognition and mood showed smaller, non-significant differences (d=-0.46 to -0.49, p=0.06-0.10). Among secondary endpoints, fatigue fell substantially more with TruBlk than with placebo, with FSS scores decreasing by 51.8% vs. 27.4% from baseline, a large between-group effect at Day 90 (d=-1.13, p<0.0001). At Day 90, 56-58% of TruBlk participants were rated "Much" or "Very Much Improved" on global assessment, compared with 12-14% of placebo. Nitric oxide showed no significant between-group difference. In an exploratory semen-analysis subset (n=57), sperm concentration increased with TruBlk relative to placebo ({delta}=0.53, p<0.001), and in a subset of 40 participants assessed for motility, total motility ({delta}=0.63, p<0.001) and progressive motility (d=0.82, p=0.014) also improved. Ninety days of standardised TruBlk Shilajit resin improved erectile function and increased total and free testosterone in men with mild-to-moderate erectile dysfunction, with improvement in several hypogonadism-related symptom domains, reduced fatigue and, in an exploratory subset, improved sperm concentration and motility. These results support standardised Shilajit resin as a promising intervention for sexual dysfunction in a clinically diagnosed population, meriting further clinical evaluation.
nb037c1dbd60c: Background: Hypothermic oxygenated perfusion (HOPE) may extend donor heart preservation beyond conventional storage durations. We evaluated early graft function and myocardial cellular and metabolic integrity following porcine heart transplantation after 20 hours of HOPE. Methods: Ten donor hearts underwent various preservation conditions: static cold storage (SCS) for 4 hours (n=2), HOPE for 4 hours (n=3), and HOPE for 20 hours (n=5), followed by heart transplantation (HT) in recipient pigs. Graft function was monitored over 3 hours by serial echocardiography, invasive hemodynamics, optical flow analysis, and vasoactive support scoring; myocardial tissue was analyzed by histopathology, flow cytometry, mitochondrial respirometry, transcriptomics, and proteomics. Results: Ejection fraction, right atrial pressure and systolic blood pressure did not differ between groups, and no graft met criteria for primary graft dysfunction. LV contractility was within normal range with comparable vasoactive support among all groups. Preservation-associated weight gain was greatest after HOPE 20h, and histopathology showed comparable findings with edema present in all cohorts, without fibrosis, thrombosis, or necrosis. Cardiomyocyte viability was preserved across all groups. Maximal oxygen consumption rate was elevated in HOPE 20h versus HOPE 4h and SCS 4h, while basal and non-mitochondrial respiration were similar. Transcriptomics and proteomics revealed limited differences in gene and pathway expression among groups. Conclusions: HOPE preserves donor heart viability, mitochondrial integrity, and ventricular function after 20 hours of preservation, without evidence of primary graft dysfunction, supporting extended preservation for heart transplantation. Edema, recovery of function, and metabolic responses warrant further investigation with longer-term monitoring.
n5df2d7582dca: Background: Previous research suggested that modifiable health factors such as physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep (i.e., 24-hour time-use behaviors) were potential intervention targets to improve antenatal depressive symptoms. However, most previous studies examine one behavior at a time, ignoring their co-dependence. The aim of this study was to examine the association between 24-hour time-use behaviors and depressive symptoms during early pregnancy. Methods: We conducted a secondary analysis using baseline data from the Health and Behaviors in Transition (HABIT) trial. Pregnant participants with pre-pregnancy body mass index [≥]25 kg/m2 wore a wrist-worn ActiGraph for seven consecutive days to estimate moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), light physical activity (LPA), inactivity (IA), and sleep. We used compositional data analysis with an isometric log-ratio transformation to examine associations with depressive symptoms, quantified by the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS), adjusting for maternal age, socioeconomic status, and cohabitation status. G-computation was applied to estimate the marginal mean of depressive symptoms at specified durations of each behavior, with the remaining time reallocated proportionally among the other behaviors. Results: A total of 255 participants with median EPDS score of 5.0 (IQR, 2.0-8.0) had geometric mean 24-hour behaviors of MVPA = 75.5 min/day (5.2%), LPA = 311.2 min/day (21.6%), IA = 593.9 min/day (41.2%), and sleep = 459.4 min/day (31.9%). 24-hour time-use behaviors were not significantly associated with EPDS scores, and marginal mean EPDS scores showed minimal changes (MVPA 10 min: 6.51 (95% CI 4.22, 9.64) vs 40 min: 5.97 (95% CI 5.03, 6.97); sleep 300 min: 5.41 (95% CI 4.56, 6.22) vs 480 min: 5.81 (95% CI 5.23, 6.39)). Conclusions: In this relatively active pregnant population, 24-hour time-use behaviors were not associated with depressive symptoms. Future research can examine later trimesters or other populations that are more sedentary or more depressed.
ndd2fc51b4f27: Background: Ultrasound is commonly used to assess hepatosplenic morbidity in schistosomiasis, but access may be limited in resource-constrained settings. Abdominal palpation is simple and inexpensive, yet its clinical value and diagnostic performance for detecting ultrasound-defined organ enlargement remains uncertain. We evaluated standardised abdominal palpation against point-of-care ultrasound in a schistosomiasis-endemic setting in rural Uganda. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional study in January-February 2024 of 3177 participants aged 5-92 years from Pakwach, Buliisa and Mayuge districts in the SchistoTrack cohort. Trained nurses who also had midwifery skills performed standardised liver and spleen palpation, assessing palpability, extension, consistency and tenderness. Palpation agreement was assessed against point-of-care B-mode ultrasound performed by sonographers with organ dimensions classified using height-standardised internal reference values. We estimated sensitivity, specificity, predictive values and Cohen's {kappa} for palpation against ultrasound-defined liver and spleen enlargement and assessed associations between liver consistency and tenderness, and schistosomal periportal fibrosis examined from ultrasound. Results: Spleen palpation had high specificity (98.4%), with sensitivity ranging from 10.9% for moderate splenomegaly to 48.6% for severe splenomegaly. There was strong agreement with ultrasound for severe splenomegaly ({kappa}=0.57) though weak agreement for moderate splenomegaly ({kappa}=0.14). Liver palpation had high specificity (97.7%) but very low sensitivity (3.4-7.3%) and minimal agreement with any hepatomegaly found from ultrasound ({kappa}=0.02-0.04).
